Studio / Styles / The Wreck of a Transport Ship

The Wreck of a Transport Ship

J. M. W. Turner, c. 1810

Oil on canvas

Storm-tossed sea in amber, brown and smoky grey, with loose, turbulent brushwork.

Use this style

J. M. W. Turner, The Wreck of a Transport Ship, c. 1810. Calouste Gulbenkian Museum, Lisbon. Source on Wikimedia Commons. Licence: Public domain.

About the painting

Turner painted this storm scene around 1810. It has long been known as The Shipwreck of the Minotaur, after a British warship lost off the Dutch coast that year, although the ship in the picture is not clearly identified. It belongs to the Calouste Gulbenkian Museum in Lisbon.

The subject is the power of the sea against the people caught in it, a central theme of Romantic painting. Turner builds the waves and spray from loose, layered paint in amber, brown and grey, and lets the light break through the storm rather than drawing every rope and spar.

How it looks on your photo

The softest style in the collection. Colours shift to warm amber and brown, edges soften, and skies take on a smoky, painted texture. It works well for moody landscapes and seascapes and for giving any photo an old varnished look.
